statement: Let k ≥ 1 and 0 ≤ q ≤ ⌊k/2⌋ be integers, put r = k − 2q, and let D = diag(θ1, . . . , θk) with θi ∈ C. For every integer m ≥ 11k − 2q, there is an m × m matrix A(X) of complex affine-linear forms such that perm(A(X)) = a0GD(X), a0 = (−2)2k (k − q)! 4 ̸= 0. (3.3) Its entrywise homogenization B(X, z) is a matrix of homogeneous linear forms whose permanent is the degree-m homogenization of a0GD: perm(B(X, z)) = a0zm−r GD(X). (3.4) The construction requires no distinctness or nonvanishing assumption on the entries of D.
